articles.title: ‘I’m sick of her talking about it’: 11 readers share how GLP-1s have affected their relationships
articles.summary: As weight loss drugs have risen all around the world, it has reshaped users’ relationships for better and for worse. As GLP-1 use continues to rise in the US and the UK, people’s bodies are being reshaped – as are their relationships.
body: “Relationships tend to develop a sense of equilibrium and predictability over time,” says Dr Lindsey Berisha, a licensed clinical psychologist who has worked with clients using GLP-1s for over 10 years. “When one partner undergoes a significant change, it can shift that equilibrium, and even positive change can create uncertainty for both partners.”

Berisha says that her clients who use GLP-1s often report feeling relieved that they are no longer consumed with thoughts of food. These users often develop more self-compassion, she says, as they realize what they previously interpreted as a failure or lack of self-control was a legitimate biological drive and food preoccupation that made life harder for them. “This shift can often be more impactful than the weight loss itself,” she says.

But these changes can elicit mixed reactions from partners, family and friends, says psychologist Dr Rachel Goldman, ranging “from being supportive to feeling insecure, left behind, or worried that the relationship itself is changing”.
points: As weight loss drugs have risen all around the world, it has reshaped users’ relationships for better and for worse.

articles.title: Young people: are you doom-saving or doom-spending? How are you approaching the future?
articles.summary: We want to hear from people under 30 about how you feel about the future and whether it’s changed the way you live your life, for better or worse. The future feels a little hard to plan for right now.
body: We’ve just lived through the hottest summer on record, global conflict looms large and AI has people wondering whether their job will still exist in five years – assuming they’ve got one in the first place.
So, with all that hanging over us, are young people simply thinking: we might as well enjoy ourselves while we can?
Or perhaps all this uncertainty has made you more cautious, more focused on getting your finances in order and determined to build a future you can rely on.
Whatever your approach, we want to hear from you. How has the state of the world changed the way you live your life?

articles.title: Your dog is bored. Here are the best tools, toys, and tips in the US to keep them enriched
articles.summary: From indoor scent training to the longest-lasting slow feeders, these are experts’ top recommendations for keeping dogs fulfilled. The best toys and tools in the US for bored indoor cats. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: A dog is much more than just a pet. They’re like family, the most eager companions for your big adventures and then the best accompaniment for an evening of snuggling up on the couch and whittling away at your Netflix queue.

At least, that’s the ideal situation. In the real world, a dog who gets too little attention and exercise or, on the flip side, is over-stimulated or over-tired, can be a real problem. There are lots of warning signs, such as a dog that is overly antsy or destructive, but Suzanne Clothier, an expert dog trainer and author of numerous books on dog enrichment, sums it up in a very simple way: “Can you watch TV or read a book in peace? If not, the dog’s telling you something.”

While there’s no one-button fix for a bored dog, advancements in enrichment toys and training are making it easier to give your little pal a fulfilled life. We spoke with five certified dog experts to get their favorite tips, tricks, toys and techniques to bolster your best buddy’s confidence and attitude.

articles.title: AI could kill all humans in next decade, warn experts: but how seriously should we take them?
articles.summary: Alarming warnings from industry insiders increase pressure for curbs on artificial superintelligence. Does artificial superintelligence really pose a risk greater than nuclear weapons? Is there a significant chance of “a Chornobyl-sized catastrophe”.
body: These warnings were issued over the past 48 hours on both sides of the Atlantic about the potential impact of a technology that most people still think of as a more talkative search engine.

Some of the threats were raised in the UK as MPs and peers began to wrestle with the danger of AI outperforming human capabilities. The nuclear warnings came from Des Browne, a former defence secretary, and Prof Stuart Russell, an eminent Berkeley computer scientist.

Beatrice Fihn, who won the 2017 Nobel peace prize for leading the International Campaign to Abolish Nuclear Weapons, told parliamentarians: “It is not the first time we’re confronted with abilities that could end up killing us all.”

The session on Monday was convened by Control AI, a lobbying group pushing for international regulation of the technology. It is backing a bill tabled in parliament this week by the Labour MP Alex Sobel and aimed at banning the creation of artificial superintelligence (ASI).

articles.title: Ashley and Mary-Kate Olsen Have Different Takes on Transeasonal Style
articles.summary: The Olsen sisters and designers made a rare appearance on the streets of New York, wearing—and carrying—multiple options for the uncertain September climate.
body: Ashley and Mary-Kate Olsen made a rare—but decidedly low-key—appearance in New York City yesterday. Despite New York Fashion Week being in full swing as of today, the sisters and The Row designers will avoid the scrum, and will take themselves to Paris for their biannual show.

First, Ashley Olsen appeared, wearing a black knit sweater with a deep V-neck and a white tank top underneath, and straight-leg black jeans on the bottom. She wore some double-strapped black sliders and oversized, angular sunglasses, and toted a smooth-grain black leather bag from her own brand.

Mary-Kate Olsen, meanwhile, opted for something a little breezier. M.K. wore a loose white t-shirt and black sweater draped over her front, paired with long, loose black shorts ( Big Shorts Summer is going nowhere, just yet). On her feet, some rare navy Yohji Yamamoto x Adidas SS2002 Prajna sneakers. (Because if they aren’t wearing The Row, the Olsens are wearing Yohji.) Over her arm, a brown croc-embossed carry-all and a pair of light-wash blue denim jeans.
points: The Olsen sisters and designers made a rare appearance on the streets of New York, wearing—and carrying—multiple options for the uncertain September climate.

articles.title: The iPhone 18 Pro Series Comes With Big Gains in Battery Life
articles.summary: While the iPhone 18 Pro looks similar to last year's model, the internals are a different story. The new A20 Pro processor with 32 Neural Engine cores will go a long way helping with on-device AI tasks—but you might not feel those differences all the time.
body: The new updates to battery life and charging, however, will make an actual difference in daily use on the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max. Apple is promising the best battery life on an iPhone yet, and is finally supporting faster wired charging.

According to Apple, the regular sized iPhone 18 Pro will have the same battery life as the outgoing, larger iPhone 17 Pro Max model, which is quite a big deal. Apple is combining the efficiency gains in the A20 Pro chip with new battery technology to deliver this large leap in battery life.
You will get 45 hours of video playback on the iPhone 18 Pro Max, and 36 hours on the iPhone 18 Pro model. The iPhone 18 Pro will last 24 hours per charge, while the 18 Pro Max can go up to 30 hours.

According to Apple, this is based on tests performed with Apple's 40W Dynamic Power Adapter with a 60W max charging speed. Wired fast charging is also supported with 60W-capable USB-C cables and USB PD 3.1 adapters that support Adjustable Voltage Supply.

articles.summary: Security updates have been trending larger, and Microsoft's Patch Tuesday for September is no exception. The company just released fixes for nearly 1,000 bugs, which is approaching double the number of flaws patched in July (the previous record).
body: Emily Long is a freelance writer based in Salt Lake City. She has nearly a decade of experience as a freelancer covering tech (including issues related to security, privacy, and streaming) as well as personal finance and travel.

In addition to Lifehacker, her work has been featured on Wirecutter, Tom’s Guide, and ZDNET. Emily has also worked as a travel guide around the U.S. and as a content editor. She has a masters in social work and is a licensed therapist in Utah.

This massive jump is in large part due to AI, which is making it easier for bad actors to develop tools to exploit vulnerabilities while also allowing developers to find and fix them more quickly. articles.title: How to Add Volume to Thin Hair, According to the Pros
articles.summary: Fine, thin hair may need some help when wanting to add volume. Here, experts break down their best tips and products on how to add volume to thin hair.
body: The main plight those with fine, thin strands have is trying to figure out how to volumize their hair. Luckily, there are a couple of ways to go about it. Celebrity hairstylist Yusef Williams says that it’s as simple as getting a good haircut (think in the form of layers or some sort of movement) or your blow-drying technique. And you have to use the right type of volumizing products to give your fine hair a lift that doesn’t look too stiff or heavy. It’s a delicate balance to give you that full, voluminous bounce of your dreams. So if you’re looking for ways to zhuzh up your hair, consider this your ultimate volumizing hair guide. Straight from the pros.

“I always say that volume starts at the root,” celebrity hairstylist Barb Thompson tells Vogue. But before you reach for any styling product, know that prepping your roots actually begins in the shower with your shampoo and conditioner. Thompson recommends starting with a lightweight shampoo and conditioner (keep conditioner mostly on the ends to not overwhelm the roots) to cleanse and create a good base.

articles.title: The 2026 CFDA Nominees and Honorees Are In—Anthony Vaccarello Named International Designer of the Year
articles.summary: From Ralph Lauren to Carolina Herrera and Public School New York, this year’s CFDA nominees represent an exciting lineup of American fashion legacies.
body: Ahead of the Council of Fashion Designers of America cocktail party tonight, followed by six full days of spring 2027 shows here in New York City—seven if you count Rachel Comey, Ralph Lauren, and Coach later today—the organization has announced its 2026 nominees and honorees. All will be celebrated at the CFDA Fashion Awards, presented by Amazon Fashion and hosted by Keke Palmer, on November 2.

Carolina Herrera’s Wes Gordon, who is celebrating the brand’s 45th anniversary this season, is nominated for a second consecutive year for American womenswear designer of the year. He joins a roster that includes two-time winner Catherine Holstein for Khaite, former winner Michael Kors, two-time nominee Tory Burch, and Diotima’s Rachel Scott, who won in 2024—a full lineup spanning generations of American fashion.

articles.title: Viva Las Lower East Side! Inside NYC’s New Vegas-Style Wedding Chapel
articles.summary: Vogue pays a visit to the newly opened Sure Thing Chapel on Allen Street to meet the couples tying the knot there—as well as Hellvis, the signature Elvis impersonator, and Tillie the Clown.
body: “Hello baby, how you doing?” growls a topless drag Satan-meets-Elvis—dubbed “Hellvis”—as his piercing blue contact-lensed eyes peek around a blush pink door on New York City’s Lower East Side. It’s a Sunday afternoon, and I’m at Sure Thing Chapel, a Las Vegas-born drive through-inspired wedding venue founded by Amy Hybarger and Victoria Hogan that has just opened its first outpost in downtown Manhattan.

Untraditional, yes. But optimistic? Always. “It’s the best gig in the world,” cooed Hellvis—a point that was echoed by his fellow officiants, Tillie the Clown, a witty and dry genderless NYC-based drag performer, and Grace, who turned to officiating after leaving over a decade working at a human rights organization in search of a more hope-filled path. “Especially in these dark times in this country and with attacks on queer people, it’s important to have love,” said Tillie.
